## Structural Analysis

The condition "for all $j \neq i, i+1$: $f(j)<f(j+1)$" means the **descent set** (positions where $f(j)>f(j+1)$) is exactly $\{i, i+1\}$ — two consecutive descents. This automatically guarantees uniqueness of $i$ (a double descent requires two consecutive descents, and the only such pair is $\{i,i+1\}$).

So $N(m,n) = \binom{m}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n-2} D(n,\{i,i+1\})$, where $D(n,S)$ counts permutations of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ with descent set exactly $S$. The count depends only on relative order, so each $n$-element subset contributes equally.

## Computing $D(n,S)$ via Inclusion-Exclusion

Using $\alpha(T) = \binom{n}{t_1,\, t_2-t_1,\, \dots,\, n-t_k}$ for descent set $\subseteq T$, and $D(n,S) = \sum_{T\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|T|}\alpha(T)$.

### $N(6,4)$: $n=4$, $\binom{6}{4}=15$ subsets

**$D(4,\{1,2\})$:** $\alpha(\{1,2\})=\binom{4}{1,1,2}=12$, $\alpha(\{1\})=4$, $\alpha(\{2\})=6$, $\alpha(\emptyset)=1$.
$$D = 12 - 4 - 6 + 1 = 3$$

**$D(4,\{2,3\})$:** By symmetry, $D = 12 - 6 - 4 + 1 = 3$.

$$N(6,4) = 15 \times (3+3) = 15 \times 6 = \mathbf{90}$$

**$D(5,\{1,2\})$:** $\alpha(\{1,2\})=\binom{5}{1,1,3}=20$, $\alpha(\{1\})=5$, $\alpha(\{2\})=10$, $\alpha(\emptyset)=1$.
$$D = 20 - 5 - 10 + 1 = 6$$

**$D(5,\{3,4\})$:** By symmetry, $D = 20 - 10 - 5 + 1 = 6$.

**$D(5,\{2,3\})$:** $\alpha(\{2,3\})=\binom{5}{2,1,2}=30$, $\alpha(\{2\})=10$, $\alpha(\{3\})=10$, $\alpha(\emptyset)=1$.
